name: Product and Fashion Mockups
title: Product and Fashion Mockups
answer: Product and fashion mockups cover the generated or composited imagery that stands in for a photograph of an object or garment before the real shoot happens. The work spans packaging renders, apparel on a model, footwear, accessories and lifestyle scenes, and it sits between commercial photography, retouching and generative image making. A mockup is judged on whether a buyer would accept it as a real photograph of the real item, so surface, seam, weave and reflection all carry weight.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Most mockup work runs on a diffusion image model, often a general purpose one such as Stable Diffusion or a hosted equivalent, paired with a control layer that fixes pose, silhouette or camera angle. Compositing and finishing happen in Photoshop or similar, and template libraries supply blank garments, bottles and packaging that the generated texture is mapped onto. The site currently tracks 1000 live image generation models, which is the pool a studio picks from when it needs a particular look or a model it can run locally.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The usual route is to start from a real product photo or a 3D base, then generate or inpaint the material, lighting and background around it. Control inputs such as depth maps, edge maps or pose skeletons keep the garment on the body and the label on the bottle, and a reference image or a trained style carries the brand look across a set. Retouchers then clean edges, match grain and colour, and check that shadows and reflections agree with the light source before the image leaves the studio.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights questions cluster around the training data, the brand assets and the model's likeness. A generated model's face can resemble a real person, a garment print can echo a protected design, and a logo placed on a mockup is a trademark use regardless of how the image was made. Provenance practice is still forming, with some studios keeping the prompt, seed, model version and source photographs on file, and disclosure of AI use is increasingly expected by clients and platforms. The site tracks 92 active intellectual property lawsuits, which is the wider backdrop against which these choices are made.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward mockups that hold up under motion and under close inspection, with video models and 3D-aware generation closing the gap to a real shoot. Consistency across a catalogue, the same garment in many colours and poses, is the practical problem most teams are working on, and reference-driven methods are the current answer. Expect more of the pipeline to move into a single tool, with the retoucher's judgement still deciding what ships.
